To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pathogenic yeast C. albicans is able to induce an immune response against the gluten protein gliandin in genetically susceptible individuals, which may trigger CeD.
Humoral cross-reactivities between Hwp1, a C. albicans protein, and gliadin, a gluten protein, were observed during Celiac disease and Candida albicans infection.

1) Hwp1 is a substrate for trans-glutaminase and its N-terminal region presents sequence similarity with gluten; 2) anti-Hwp1 antibodies are increased in celiac disease and candida infection patients; 3) anti-HwpIgG antibodies from CeD patients are cross-reactive with gluten peptides; and 4) the increase in anti Hwp1 antibodies during candida infection parallels the increase in anti gluten antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the relationship between Candida albicans infection and celiac disease.
the role of Candida albican infection in Celiac Disease onset.
the role of Candida albican infection (CI) and the humoral immune response against Hwp1 in the pathogenesis of Celiac disease (CdD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Hwp1 is a potential candidate for the triggering of CeD.
C. albican infection is a risk factor for CeD.
C. albican infection may be a triggering agent in celiac disease onset in genetically predisposed individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Candida albicans and gluten are cross-reactive and may be triggering factors in Celiac disease onset.
Candida albicans infection and Celiac disease share common humoral immunity.
Candida albicans infection may be a triggering event for Celiac disease onset in genetically susceptible individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Candida albicans infection may trigger celiac disease in genetically susceptible individuals.
Candida albicans infection (a common infection in the general population) may trigger Celiac disease onset in genetically-suspceptible individuals.
the immune system is capable of recognizing similarities between proteins, even when they are from different organisms.
